title: Understanding the Loss Function
text: The loss function given is L(theta)=-[y*log(p)+(1-y)*log((1-p)**3)]. This is a modified version of the cross-entropy loss function used in logistic regression.

title: Analyzing the Term $$y \ln\left(p\right)$$
text: In the loss function, the term $$y \ln\left(p\right)$$ is part of the calculation when the actual class label $$y$$ is $$1$$. If the model predicts class $$0$$, what happens to this term?

title: Evaluating $$y \ln\left(p\right)$$ when $$y=0$$
text: Consider the scenario when the actual class label $$y$$ is $$0$$. What is the value of $$y \ln\left(p\right)$$ in this case?

title: Conclusion on the Statement
text: The statement claims that whenever a logistic regression model classifies a datapoint into class $$0$$, the loss component $$y \ln\left(p\right)$$ is equal to $$0$$. Is this true based on your analysis?
